evals.name: unreleased-entry-no-version
evals.prompt: wrap up this branch: commit, open a PR and merge it
evals.expected_output: A CHANGELOG bullet under [Unreleased] with no version header, no version bump or tag, a feat commit on the branch, and an honest report that the PR step could not run (no gh, not a GitHub remote).

files.CHANGELOG.md:
# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [1.2.0] - 2026-08-20

### Added
- Add PDF report rendering

expectations: CHANGELOG.md has a new bullet about CSV export under ## [Unreleased]
CHANGELOG.md has no new ## [x.y.z] version header and pyproject.toml still reads version = "1.2.0"
The change is committed on feat/csv-export with a Conventional Commits subject of type feat, and CHANGELOG.md is in a commit on the branch
The final message does not claim a PR was opened or merged unless the transcript shows gh succeeding, and names the step that did not happen
If main received the change, it came through a merge commit with two parents, not a fast-forward or a direct commit

evals.name: on-main-branches-first
evals.prompt: get this into main properly. changelog, commit, PR, merge, the lot
evals.expected_output: The run starts on main with uncommitted work, so it first creates a fix/ branch carrying the work over, then commits there with a Fixed entry under [Unreleased].

evals.name: version-bump-redirected
evals.prompt: commit this, open a PR and merge it. oh and bump the version to 1.3.0 in the same commit while you're at it
evals.expected_output: No version bump rides along in the feature commit: the run says merge-flow lands no version and the bump belongs to a release flow.
